and compiled. Use the [finite caller](RENDERER_BRACKET_CONSUMER.md) and
[adoption handoff](handoffs/autonomy-restart-20261011.md). The staging/install
instructions below are historical; do not apply the old patch to a completed run.
Actual driver behavior remains unverified.

This source-only change unlocks the next distinct26.2 Fabric MakeUp private
submission-copy comparison. It preserves the existing finite runner, immutable
input/freezes, source ancestry, quality and Off restoration checks. It does not
launch a client or reopen the closed1.21.11 MakeUp trial.

MINIMIZED and0invalid frames. Its5.885→7.414→12.790ms/render bracket has117.33%

and effective120/NONE between good260 snapshots. The patch pins the cap at the
start of the actual measured window, latches a rejected frame on any change,
retains configured/effective bounds and observation count, and preserves an
unavailable observation in the completed-render denominator. Early failure
receipts preserve the partial window counts and explicitly invalidate the whole
measurement. No frame is selected out, input timer reset or pacing simulated.

  Existing loaded native100/AA, command consumption, freeze, still and restoration
  assertions remain in place.
- Qualification failure retains the raw receipt and qualified error output.
  Extending a comparison requires scientific review of the actual avoided-work
  denominator and both original comparisons. No automatic rerun or numeric drift
  threshold is introduced.

# BSL viewport property correction R6

2026-10-07; owner `bsl_viewport_contract`. Scope: only
`patches/experiments/bsl-real-budget-r1/build.py`, this report, and isolated ignored
`dev/logs/bsl-viewport-r6/` outputs. Parent owns observer pins, build/runtime,
client/GPU and checkpoints. No client, Gradle, encoder, download or background
process was started. No runtime reload is authorized by this report.

## Failure and exact shipped contract

R5's first guarded producer viewport was `[0, 0, 1920, 1200]`, while the intended
viewport was 960 × 600. It remains a failed work-area observation, without quality
or performance acceptance. Original receipt:
`dev/logs/bsl-work-area-r5/observation/work-area.json`, SHA256
`bee188b18bc0027654917bfb9a0e2ce7c8d5d1e576df77de1eb1de021eeecf94`.

Examined the actual shipped
`dev/runtime/iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar`, SHA256
`3e3f94d2d5cdcb8145c4385d521974aa2d8669b2cc212351f70cf06488182e83`,
using `javap -c -p`; no syntax was guessed from another Iris release.

- `ShaderProperties.handlePassDirective` strips exactly the `scale.` prefix using
  `substring(prefix.length())`; it does not strip dimension directories. The scale
  lambda inserts that remaining string directly into `viewportScaleOverrides`.
- `ProgramSet.readProgramArray` passes prefix plus numeric suffix as the program
  name, independently of `AbsolutePackPath`. Index zero has an empty suffix.
  `ProgramArrayId.Deferred` obtains base name `deferred` from `ProgramGroup`.
  `readProgramSource` passes that bare name into `ProgramSource`'s constructor.
- `ProgramDirectives` uses
  `getViewportScaleOverrides().getOrDefault(program.getName(), ViewportData.defaultValue())`.
  The default is `(scale=1.0, viewportX=0.0, viewportY=0.0)`.
- `CompositeRenderer` multiplies its pass width/height by that scale, converts to
  integer dimensions, and calls `RenderSystem.viewport` before drawing.

Therefore `scale.world0/deferred=0.5` stores key `world0/deferred`, which does not
match the actual producer name `deferred`. The corresponding supported key is
`scale.deferred=0.5`. This binary result explains the R5 full viewport; corrected
actual GL behavior still needs a new guarded runtime observation.

Exact bytecode evidence, all under `dev/logs/bsl-viewport-r6/`:
`iris-bytecode.txt` (ProgramSource, ProgramDirectives, ShaderProperties,
ProgramSet, CompositeRenderer), `iris-array-viewport-bytecode.txt`
(ProgramArrayId, ViewportData), and `iris-program-group-bytecode.txt`.

# Development camera quality capture

`src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/dev/CameraQualitySession.java` is the integrated
development capture utility. It compiled and completed bounded runtime smokes
recorded below, including the fast lossless writer's 603 native frames; broader
quality acceptance remains pending. Loaded-only camera contracts have since
rendered in the targeted checks. The new optional two-image backpressure change
is source-only until root compiles and retries native capture. This change owns
only the capture session, new pure `CaptureWriteTracker`/fixture and this
document. The observer, PNG writer, common protocol, shaders, build settings,
client processes and old raw captures are untouched by this worker.

The harness addresses the missing moving-camera quality check for original,
derivative-off and derivative-on packs. It records quality evidence only.
Framebuffer readback, PNG compression, disk writes and fingerprinting affect
timing. Its frame counters and wall times identify source frames and capture
gaps; they must not be analyzed as a GPU/FPS speedup.

## Activation and integration

Only `shaderlod.dev.cameraQuality` activates it. Its value is the path of a
local JSON request, read once and limited to 64 KiB. An absent/blank property
returns `null` without opening files, creating threads or moving the player.
`shaderlod.dev.cameraQualityOnly=true` additionally authorizes stopping this
same client after the final manifest and PNG callback handling. The session
must have acquired its local spectator UUID; a rejected request does not close
an unacquired client.

Both capture classes belong only in the dev client source set; verify they and
their nested classes remain absent from the production jar. The integrated
hooks in `ComparisonClient` have this shape:

```java
private CameraQualitySession cameraQuality;

// In the existing one-time configured block, after scene/control preparation:
cameraQuality = CameraQualitySession.createIfRequested(
        client.gameDirectory.toPath());

// After applyControl() in ClientTickEvent.Post, before normal workload handling:
if (cameraQuality != null) {
    cameraQuality.tick(client);
    GpuTimers.drainSamples();
    CpuTimers.drainSamples();
    return;
}

// At the START of draw(RenderGuiEvent.Post), before hideGui's early return:
if (cameraQuality != null) {
    event.getGuiGraphics().flush();
    cameraQuality.render(Minecraft.getInstance());
}
```

The owner must gate creation of `WorkloadSession` and `BenchmarkSession` when
the explicit camera-quality property is present, and place the tick branch
before both old manual/automatic screenshot schedules. The configured block
must preserve the prepared ShaderLOD settings rather than apply its ordinary
comparison enable/preset defaults. A rejected request must retain
its rejection manifest and must not silently become a benchmark. Use a
dedicated quality launch; do not enable `measureWorkload`, `measureOnly`,
`benchmark` or `benchmarkOnly` in that launch. The ordinary comparison client
still opens the prepared landscape world and applies its existing control.
Original absent-mod runs use the existing `compare=off` dev client.

If launching through Gradle, forward these two project properties explicitly
in the dev run configuration; Gradle JVM properties do not automatically reach
the game JVM:

```groovy
if (project.hasProperty('cameraQuality')) {
    systemProperty 'shaderlod.dev.cameraQuality', project.property('cameraQuality').toString()
}
if (project.hasProperty('cameraQualityOnly')) {
    systemProperty 'shaderlod.dev.cameraQualityOnly', project.property('cameraQualityOnly').toString()
}
```
